entries.reason: Derived group bindings retain generation handles and order values, with owning immutable canonical keys rather than ECS or group pointers.
entries.ownership: RTS remains the sole authoritative group/member/order owner. The flow service owns a replaceable derived handle/order projection; each collected Route owns immutable goal data and captures Crowd owner/input epoch.
entries.restore: Group projection rebuilds from validated membership. Fresh Crowd owner or input revision prevents reuse of old bindings/routes. Terminal phase is derived, regenerated after restore; no bit-exact persistent continuation claim.
entries.stale: Member lookup compares full table/type/id/generation plus current order binding. Route consumption validates Crowd owner/input before modifying AgentUpdate. No callbacks or ECS structural mutation occur during projection publication.
entries.create: RTS group phase stages the complete validated membership/slot projection. Motion collects owning routes for generation-checked current View members and matching orders.
entries.destroy_order: Unit-first destruction or replacement invalidates the generation handle; current View/order validation excludes old members. Group-first removal replaces the projection; no group address is retained. Service destruction drops derived bindings and plans; already collected owning values retain no provider pointer.

entries.write_set: motion, orders, lifecycle projections, production queues, faction research state, match participant/state/event components and affected surrender roots; RTS-owned movement-group membership and rebuilt Navigation formation speed projection; derived shared-goal jobs and lease assignments, Navigation pending/unreachable projection and Motion arrival. Derived group bindings and monotonic terminal-route phase are atomically replaced outside views. Navigation combatSlotTarget/combatSlotWaiting are tick-expiring derived projections, committed after a complete owning plan and excluded from snapshots.
entries.structural_changes: unit production and surrender collect stable handles during traversal, then create or destroy only after the relevant view closes
entries.events: ordered command, production, effect, technology unlock, surrender and victory lifecycle facts are emitted after authoritative mutation; static-flow unreachable notifications are deferred until successful movement projection and resolve typed handles before callbacks.
entries.services: injected SimulationStep, definition registry, action executor, resource query and capability services; callbacks are synchronous and not retained; explicitly configured CrowdFlowNavigation owner service, deterministic per-tick start/work quotas.
entries.phase: owner-thread deterministic simulation after command ingestion and before presentation; match evaluation follows authoritative economy settlement; shared navigation planning precedes group projection, one quota pump, Crowd motion and post-commit notices. Infantry slot admission precedes both native and Crowd motion; rear admission suppresses firing in existing CombatFireSystem.

entries.reason: Explicit shared-goal policy deduplicates eligible linked movement navigation and publishes immutable leases at the motion boundary.
protocol: Owning in-process quota configuration; exact script integer quotas; derived jobs/leases/group routes are not persistent identities. Pending/unreachable does not complete an order.
Unreachable notices own OrderRecord plus generation handle, moved out before callbacks after motion success. Order-reported flag changes at committed delivery; stale handles skip delivery.

Attack/Escort/Patrol use movementGoal. Constrained movement groups share canonical slot sets, then keep a bounded singleton terminal route after entering any slot cell. Open radius-clear moving slots, traffic recovery and threat-overlay supply routes remain explicit policies.

Group preparation copies and normalizes keys once per group. Current caps: 64 group projections, 1024 members/targets per group, 10000 queued goal keys and 64 simultaneously retained builders. Queue metadata is bounded separately from field workspaces; excess builder demand remains observable Pending in admission order. Queue overflow fails explicitly and never runs synchronous A*.

Within one navigation service instance, one positive pump attempt per owner/tick, including failure. Same-owner input repair does not refund quota. Failed preparation attempts count; failed graph work charges its reserved quantum and cancels the partial builder. New restored owner starts a new timeline.

RTS retains one service across configure/clear for spending continuity. Quota changes preserve jobs; equal configuration is NoOp. Disable releases jobs/leases, keeps the owner/tick latch, exposes empty status and stops all shared-policy consumers. Clear-agent-lease sync also executes after immediate re-enable.

CrowdMotionSystem reserves selected output frame capacity and freezes owning OrderRecord projections before advance; copyAgentStates reuses that capacity after join. SharedFlow pending does not publish arrived before successful motion. All ECS poses publish before dynamic-goal arrival evaluation. Native parallel-consumer tests cover 300 units, provider expiration, gather rollback, pending arrival failure, and target creation-order parity. Arrival idle candidates and zero/one selection storage are canonically prepared before advance. After pose/arrival computation, commitAgentUpdates applies only selected idle intents without success-path workspace allocation. Preparation failure does not consume motion; worker failure discards the owning token. Numeric identities remain stable across advance.
entries.thread_affinity: Known owner-thread flow service; retains owned numeric goals/plans/leases only, not ECS pointers. View pointers live only during the motion call. Source owner/input epochs reset derived jobs after restore or terrain changes. Notice callbacks run after motion/view closure; receiver handles revalidate, callbacks cannot reenter step or destroy RTS.
